scenario: A big cheerful round Nucleus character, the librarian at the heart of the cell, covered in small round button-like portholes (nuclear pore complexes) sitting flat on its surface. Through one porthole it hands a small friendly scroll character (a copied instruction) to a waiting round Ribosome character. A cutaway window shows a smaller round Nucleolus character stacking bead-shaped ribosome parts. Soft cloud shapes (chromatin) and simple squiggle loops fill the rest of the body. A wavy bumpy ribbon character (rough ER) is attached seamlessly at the lower-left and runs off the frame. Zoomed in close so the big ball itself is cut off by all four edges, with a few background Ribosome-friend circles cut off in the corners.

command: uv run --script .claude/skills/microbe-render/scripts/coloring.py --microbe nucleus --set organelles --prompt-file <this prompt, v3> --speech-en "Copies only - the original never leaves!" --speech-de "Nur Kopien - das Original bleibt hier!" --attempt 3
prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080. Composition must be SQUARE, never wide or landscape. Composition is ZOOMED IN CLOSE: the main character fills almost the whole frame and every surrounding character runs past the picture edge.

CRITICAL — READ FIRST: (a) the drawing must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES with NO frame, NO border line, NO box and NO white margin band — big shapes must touch and cross every one of the four edges; (b) draw ONLY smooth closed outlines and simple round polka-dot portholes sitting flat on surfaces — do NOT draw any pointed rays, spikes, sparkle shapes or starburst shapes anywhere in the picture, not even small ones, not behind any character and not around any character.

SCENE: A cheerful round NUCLEUS character is the friendly librarian at the heart of a busy cell, handing out copies of instructions.
- The NUCLEUS CHARACTER is one big, round, plump ball filling most of the frame, with a big happy round face in the middle: two large round eyes with pupils, cheerful eyebrows and a wide open smile. Its outer edge is a smooth double outline — draw the ball's outline as two closely-spaced smooth curved lines running all the way around it like the rim of a thick round cushion, with a thin white gap between the two lines.
- Dotted evenly all over the ball's round body, draw many small simple ROUND PORTHOLES (like round portholes on a ship, or big friendly buttons) sitting flat on the surface — each porthole a small plain circle with one smaller circle inside it. Keep every porthole small, round and flat against the body. These portholes must read as calm polka-dot buttons resting ON the ball, never as pointed rays, never as a burst, never as spikes or beams shooting outward.
- Through one large open porthole near the middle-right of the body, the Nucleus character is cheerfully handing out a small friendly SCROLL CHARACTER (a short curled ribbon of paper with two dot eyes and a smile) to a small round ROBOT-LIKE RIBOSOME character waiting just outside the porthole, its little round arms reaching up to take the scroll.
- Inside the Nucleus, visible through a large soft round cutaway window on its body, sits a smaller round NUCLEOLUS character with its own happy round face, busily stacking a few small bead-shaped ribosome-part characters into a neat pile in front of it, like a baker stacking buns.
- Around the cutaway window, fill the rest of the Nucleus body with a few big soft cloud-shaped puffy patches near the outer rim (friendly bundled-up chromatin clouds, each a simple rounded scalloped outline) and a few short simple squiggly loops floating in the open middle area (relaxed, unrolled chromatin loops) — keep every squiggle a plain closed wavy line, no sharp points.
- Attached smoothly to the lower-left side of the Nucleus, with no seam or gap, a friendly wavy RIBBON character (the rough endoplasmic reticulum) folds gently across the corner of the frame, cut off by the edge; it has simple round bumps dotted along its outer edge and its own small happy dot-eyed face near where it joins the Nucleus, showing that the two characters are one connected body.
- BACKGROUND, filling the remaining corners and running off the edges: a couple of small round free-floating RIBOSOME characters with simple faces, and a loose scatter of small plain circles and tiny dots — everything large, simple, chunky and cut off by the frame, with generous open white space inside every shape for a child to colour.

STYLE — coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only).
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with plenty of white space.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN — the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, motion rays or halo of rays behind, around or under any character or any porthole. NO radiating or pointed lines of any kind anywhere.
- ANY rectangle, rounded rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box, shelf, table or vignette. The drawing must NOT sit inside a box of any kind. Do NOT draw a thin black line anywhere near the edge of the image. There must be NO white margin between the artwork and the image edge.
- The artwork must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES of the square — the ribbon character and the background circles are CUT OFF by the image edge itself.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels or watermarks anywhere. The scroll character carries no writing.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO condensed X-shaped chromosome shapes anywhere — only the soft cloud clumps and simple loops described above.
- NO human figures, no hands (other than the small round ribosome character's simple stub arms), no arrows.

CRITICAL SIZE FIX (read carefully — two previous attempts got this wrong): draw the Nucleus ball SO BIG that its round double-outline edge is CUT OFF by ALL FOUR EDGES of the square at once — top, bottom, left AND right — the same way a photo that is zoomed in very close crops off the subject on every side. Do not leave a plain white margin band along the top edge or the right edge; instead let the ball's own curved outline, or one of its portholes, or a background character, physically touch and cross every one of the four edges, corner areas included. The face, portholes, cutaway window and ribbon must all still fit inside this much larger ball, even if that means the very outer rim of the ball itself runs past the top and right edges of the picture and is no longer fully visible. Small background circles may fill any leftover sliver of white, but they must also touch the edges, not float in the middle of empty margins.
